ev-20fca8134e.rationale: Consistency only, not a provider rule. Two open-source rule artifacts from different maintainers, each pinned to a commit, both define the glpat- legacy token body as 20 characters (word characters and hyphen in the first; alphanumerics, hyphen, equals and underscore, 20 to 22 long, in the second); the value 'glpat-abc123' has 6 characters after the prefix, so it falls outside that grammar in both. GitLab's token overview (docs.gitlab.com/security/tokens/) states the glpat- prefix but no body length, so no provider-documented basis exists for the length. Scanner output on this fixture and agreement between scanners are not used.

sources.supports: Rule gitlab-pat (v8.30.1) matches glpat- followed by exactly 20 characters in \w and hyphen; consistent with a 6-character body not being a complete token.
Detector gitlab v2 (v3.97.4) matches glpat- followed by 20 to 22 characters in [a-zA-Z0-9\-=_]; consistent with a 6-character body not being a complete token.
